date_note: SANS diary published Nov 16; picked up Nov 18.
title: SANS honeypots see scans for chained LiteLLM and Starlette flaws (CVE-2026-42271, CVE-2026-48710)
summary: SANS ISC honeypots recorded requests to /mcp-rest/test/tools/list attempting to chain CVE-2026-42271 in LiteLLM with CVE-2026-48710 in Starlette for unauthenticated remote code execution. Starlette before 1.0.1 does not validate the Host header. SANS cites a Horizon3.ai write-up and says exploitation has been reported since July. Whether any attempts succeeded is not stated.
plain: Researchers see attackers probing internet-facing LiteLLM servers, a popular gateway for AI models, using two chained flaws that could let them run code without logging in.
exec: LiteLLM often holds AI provider keys; exposed instances are already being probed and a public technique exists.
action: Upgrade Starlette to 1.0.1 or later, update LiteLLM, keep LiteLLM off the public internet, and rotate provider keys on any exposed instance.
